title: Certify the source-derived continuation PC envelope and admission boundary
body:
The historical PR2753/PR589 selected caller still derives its continuation bound with Python `len(operations)`, even though its source word exceeds the host index range. This package derives its actual source length envelope without enumerating GL64 classes or residual factories:

`12,295,296 G + 78,175 <= N <= 59,884,739,136 G + 78,175`, where `G=|GL64(F_q)|` at the inherited prime. This gives a continuation width between 359,385 and 359,398 bits.

The proof counts the actual 288 calls, hosted idle remainder requests and all good/fallback Cursor possibilities. It binds the bound to unchanged FiniteFields/Tape and literal source call/return header statements, with exact codec costs. An upper bound does not supply exact instruction indexing and may admit forged PCs beyond the true length; the package states the exact provider/domain validation still required and does not ship an unsupported count-for-len adapter.

Validation: 318 actual source plan/Cursor cases, normal/optimized replay, source successor/stage controls, typed/missing receipt and source-byte rejection, committed source-history check, explicit-base export and Git-free empty-PATH normal/optimized replay. Header tests are projected statement fixtures, not selected recursive payload execution. This historical caller result is not admission of the current PR5413 supplier, a stock/tariff improvement or a new kappa.

Canonical investigation: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-19173371

JoyboyBrian, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Retains Jose Manuel's source compiler/caller/codec and PR2234 prime witness, predecessor attribution and Apache-2.0.
